title: Designing Reliable Electronics Prototypes
summary: A practical workflow for moving from a circuit idea to a tested, documented prototype.
body: A reliable prototype starts with a clear boundary: define the inputs, outputs, power requirements, and failure conditions before choosing components.
Break the design into small testable blocks. Validate power, communication, and sensor paths separately, then combine them after each block behaves as expected.
Document the decisions while you build. A short test log makes debugging faster and turns a one-off experiment into a reusable engineering process.

title: Learning Through Real Engineering Projects
summary: Why small, complete builds create deeper technical understanding than isolated tutorials.
body: Projects create useful constraints. They force hardware, software, documentation, and testing to work together instead of leaving knowledge in separate lessons.
Choose a build that is small enough to finish but rich enough to expose one real engineering tradeoff. A finished project gives you evidence you can inspect and improve.
The goal is not perfect first attempts. The goal is a repeatable cycle of building, measuring, learning, and refining.

title: Notes on Digital Systems and Interfaces
summary: The design habits that make UART, SPI, I2C, and memory-controller work easier to reason about.
body: Digital interfaces become easier to debug when timing, ownership, and reset behavior are written down before implementation.
Use small simulations and targeted test cases to verify one protocol rule at a time. This keeps failures local and makes waveforms useful rather than overwhelming.
Good interface design is communication between engineers as much as it is communication between devices.
